ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Two harmonic transverse waves propagate along the positive and negative directions of the $x$-axis, respectively. The wave sources are located at $x=-0.2\mathrm{m}$ and $x=1.2\mathrm{m}$, with both waves having a wave speed of $0.4\mathrm{m/s}$ and an amplitude of $2\mathrm{m}$. The figure shows the images of the two waves at time $t=0$. At this moment, the particles $P$ and $Q$ at the equilibrium positions $x=0.2\mathrm{m}$ and $x=0.8\mathrm{m}$ in the medium just begin to vibrate. The equilibrium position of particle $M$ is located at $x=0.5\mathrm{m}$.

1. At what time do the two waves meet?
2. What is the distance traveled by the mass element M during the time interval from 0s to 1.5s?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: In the figure at t = 0, the left wave occupies the interval from x = -0.2 m to x = 0.2 m and is marked with an arrow moving in the +x direction; its leading front is at P, x = 0.2 m. The right wave occupies the interval from x = 0.8 m to x = 1.2 m and is marked with an arrow moving in the -x direction; its leading front is at Q, x = 0.8 m. Point M is marked at x = 0.5 m, halfway between P and Q. From the plotted zero-to-zero pattern, each wave spans one full wavelength of 0.4 m. Reasoning: The two leading fronts are separated by 0.8 - 0.2 = 0.6 m and move toward each other with relative speed 0.4 + 0.4 = 0.8 m/s, so they meet after 0.6 / 0.8 = 0.75 s, at M. Before t = 0.75 s, M has not started vibrating. From t = 0.75 s to t = 1.5 s, M vibrates for 0.75 s. The period is T = λ / v = 0.4 / 0.4 = 1 s, so M vibrates for 3T/4. The two waves reach M simultaneously and have matching phase there, so the resultant amplitude is 2A = 4 m. During 3T/4, the displacement changes 0 -> -4 m -> 0 -> +4 m, so the total distance traveled is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 m.
